mentl/a414804:
Strings are no longer always [len][bytes...] flat. Two shapes, one
interface:

  FLAT — [len_i32 >= 0][bytes...]
    Constructed by alloc + mem_copy; produced by str_concat,
    int_to_str, seed data-section literals.

  VIEW — [-1_sentinel][buf_ptr][start_offset][length]
    Reference into a flat string's payload. Constructed by
    str_slice. 16-byte header alloc; ZERO byte-copy regardless
    of slice length. Result of view_base on a view is always
    (flat_buf, absolute_offset) — view chains collapse at slice
    time so byte_at remains O(1).

Eight interrogations cleared (per docs/SUBSTRATE.md + DESIGN.md
ultimate-medium principles):
- Graph: source bytes encoded at their original buffer; views
  point back rather than copy
- Handler: +Memory for byte_at; +Alloc only at concat/output
  boundaries — slice is +Alloc(16), not +Alloc(N)
- Verb: |> sequential walk via byte_at; no copy in the chain
- Row: orders of magnitude lower alloc — N-byte slice was N+4
  bytes, now 16 bytes regardless of N
- Ownership: views borrow; concat materializes (owns the
  new flat buffer)
- Refinement: view carries (start, length) bounds on buf
- Gradient: future ops stay zero-copy through chained slices
  via view_base collapse
- Reason: provenance preserved — view's buf field IS the source

`is_view(s) = load_i32(s) < 0` discriminates without bitwise ops
(Mentl has no bitwise primitive yet — only logical &&; the -1
sentinel sidesteps that and produces the same dispatch).

str_concat uses mem_copy on view_base-resolved (buf, off) pairs —
hot-path bulk-copy via the existing mem_copy primitive; routes
view/flat operands uniformly through view_base.

Substrate replaces the bootstrap discipline "strings always flat"
documented in CLAUDE.md. The change is ABI-compatible at the
observer level: every byte_at / byte_len caller works unchanged;
only str_slice's payload shape changes (always view now).

two-top/a4fe499:
Choosing a table used to mean a text line that cycled blind on tap,
couch-only, keys 1-3 covering three of seven arenas; online the room
URL's hash decided, which also silently pinned every quick match to ONE
arena forever (the public room string never changes). All of that goes.

The roster: a real select screen (AppScreen::ArenaSelect) - seven rows,
each showing its actual floor as the thumbnail, its name, and one line
of the rules that make it that arena. Tap the arena line on the Title
(couch AND online) or press A to open it; 1-7 pick directly on the
roster and on the couch title (the online title's digits still belong
to the room pad and name dial). The pick persists in the settings JSON
and TWOTOP_ARENA overrides it for capture automation.

Online agreement is structural now: the pick joins the room NAME
(two-top-pit?next=2, two-top-CURS-pit?next=2), composed by a
change-detection sync whenever the dial or the pick moves. Two peers in
one room cannot disagree about the table, the arena is known before
anything spawns, and no new netcode ships. Quick match partitions by
arena - with this player pool that is a feature, and friends already
coordinate codes out loud: dial CURS, pick the Pit. arena_from_room and
its FNV hash are deleted.

Cover stops being the same gray box everywhere: cover_skin() gives each
arena its face and lid colors plus one quiet lid motif (crate lashing,
pillar flutes, the sealed teal seam, an ember crack, the plinth's lit
rim). The flat-quad depth composite stays - identity comes from the
register, not from noise.

Docs: PLAYBOOK and SIGNALING carry the room-name convention (both
phones must pick the same arena to meet), MORGAN_NOTES the chasm and
room-name rationale, CLAUDE.md the refreshed facts (513 tests, v13).
two-top/a41624b:
Refactors advance_animation to delegate to a new pure helper
next_anim_state(dead, dash, stun, current) -> AnimState. The
helper holds 100% of the state-machine logic; the system is now
a thin loop. This makes the state machine property-testable
without spinning up a Bevy World per case.

7 property tests cover structural invariants:
- next_anim_is_deterministic — pure-function determinism
- death_priority_overrides_all — Dead.is_dying() always wins
- hit_priority_overrides_dash_and_idle_and_throw — non-zero
  StunFrames preempts everything except DEATH
- transition_resets_ticks — anim_id change always resets ticks=0
- continuation_increments_ticks_by_one — same-anim ticks++ exactly
- throw_one_shot_runs_to_completion_when_unpreempted — THROW
  in flight stays THROW unless DEATH/HIT preempts
- display_index_in_atlas_range — output never escapes [0, 21]

Plus 4 targeted regression tests:
- idle_alive_unstunned_not_dashing_lands_idle
- fresh_dash_transition_resets_ticks
- hit_preempts_throw_one_shot
- death_caps_at_last_frame_via_display_index

proptest = "1.11" added as a sim dev-dependency (same pin as
fixed_math). 11 new tests total; workspace suite goes from 261
to 272 tests, all passing. clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

This is the kind of test that catches subtle bugs LONG before
operator validation finds them — e.g. a refactor that breaks
HIT-preempts-THROW would surface here as a failed proptest
minimization rather than as confused player feedback weeks later.
